topic.name: Representing Solutions to Inequalities on Number Lines

question.text: Represent the solution of the inequality $2x + 9 \gt 1$ on a number line.
question.explanation:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $9$ from both sides:

\begin{align} 2x + 9 &> 1 \\[5pt] 2x + 9 - 9 &> 1 - 9 \\[5pt] 2x + 0 &> -8 \\[5pt] 2x &> -8 \end{align}

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $2{:}$

\begin{align} \require{cancel} 2x &> -8 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2x}{2} &> \dfrac{-8}2 \\[5pt] \dfrac{\cancel{2}x}{\cancel{2}} &> \dfrac{-8}2 \\[5pt] x &> -4 \end{align}

Therefore, the solution is $x > -4.$ The solution can be expressed on a number line, as shown below.

question.text: Represent the solution of the inequality $5x - 3 \lt 2$ on a number line.
question.explanation:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $3$ to both sides:

\begin{align} 5x - 3 &\lt 2 \\[5pt] 5x - 3 + 3 &\lt 2 + 3 \\[5pt] 5x + 0 &\lt 5 \\[5pt] 5x &\lt 5 \end{align}

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $5{:}$

\begin{align} \require{cancel} 5x &\lt 5 \\[5pt] \dfrac{5x}{5} &\lt \dfrac55 \\[5pt] \dfrac{\cancel{5}x}{\cancel{5}} &\lt \dfrac55 \\[5pt] x &\lt 1 \end{align}

Therefore, the solution is $x \lt 1.$ The solution can be expressed on a number line, as shown below.

question.text: Represent the solution of the inequality $2 \gt 3x + 5$ on a number line.
question.explanation:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $5$ from both sides:

\begin{align} 2 &> 3x + 5 \\[5pt] 2 - 5 &> 3x + 5 - 5 \\[5pt] -3 &> 3x + 0 \\[5pt] -3 &> 3x \end{align}

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $3{:}$

\begin{align} \require{cancel} -3 &> 3x \\[5pt] \dfrac{-3}{3} &> \dfrac{3x}3 \\[5pt] \dfrac{-3}{3} &> \dfrac{\cancel{3}x}{\cancel{3}} \\[5pt] -1 &> x \end{align}

Finally, let's swap the left and right-hand sides so that the variable is on the left-hand side. Remember, we also need to flip the inequality. \[ x < -1 \] Therefore, the solution is $x < -1.$ The solution can be expressed on a number line, as shown below.
